name: Question 10
worked_solution:
We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{8{x}^{7}}{{(5+{x}^{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{8{x}^{7}}{{(5+{x}^{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{8{x}^{7}}{{(5+{x}^{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x
$$

First, we calculate the antiderivative using a substitution. Let  $u=5+{x}^{8}$,  then $\text{d}u=8{x}^{7}\text{d}x.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8{x}^{7}}{{(5+{x}^{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{u}+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{5+{x}^{8}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We now evaluate the first of the improper integrals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{8{x}^{7}}{{(5+{x}^{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{8{x}^{7}}{{(5+{x}^{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{(-\frac{1}{5+{x}^{8}})|}_{a}^{0} \\  & =-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{5+0}-\frac{1}{5+{a}^{8}}) \\  & =-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{5+{a}^{8}}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}+0 \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand is an **odd** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{8{x}^{7}}{{(5+{x}^{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{8{x}^{7}}{{(5+{x}^{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{8{x}^{7}}{{(5+{x}^{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{8{x}^{7}}{{(5+{x}^{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{5} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We break up the integral as follows: ∫−∞∞8x7(5+x8)2dx=∫−∞08x7(5+x8)2dx+∫0∞8x7(5+x8)2dx

First, we calculate the antiderivative using a substitution. Let u=5+x8, then du=8x7dx. Hence,

∫8x7(5+x8)2dx=∫1u2du=−1u+C=−15+x8+C.

We now evaluate the first of the improper integrals, as follows:

∫−∞08x7(5+x8)2dx=lima→−∞∫a08x7(5+x8)2dx=lima→−∞(−15+x8)|a0=−lima→−∞(15+0−15+a8)=−lima→−∞(15−15+a8)=−15+0=−15

Now, notice that the integrand is an odd function. This means that we can immediately deduce that

∫0∞8x7(5+x8)2dx=15.

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that ∫−∞∞8x7(5+x8)2dx=∫−∞08x7(5+x8)2dx+∫0∞8x7(5+x8)2dx=−15+15=0.
